title: Prompt affinity decomposition and hotpatch notes
summary: Working notes for a focused failure decomposition on onboarding eval regressions that cluster by prompt affinity rather than semantic category. Goal: identify compact hotpatches for serving-time mitigations and a prioritized list of longer term onboarding fixes.
problem_statement: During onboarding evals for v2 candidate models we observed a ~9-12% drop on the 'appropriateness' rubric relative to the baseline for a subset of prompt families. Failures are concentrated in a small number of prompt affinities (format/intent scaffolding) rather than purely topical clusters. Need targeted, low-risk mitigations that can be deployed as config or prompt-layer patches to avoid blocking rollout.
dataset_and_eval_context: Eval corpus: 18k mixed-domain promptset used for onboarding (seeded from customer logs + synthetic augment). Model under test: community-llm-7b-qkv-v2. Metrics: Pairwise human ratings (helpfulness, factuality, appropriateness), automated toxicity check, token-penalty cost. Baseline: production-stable-1. Test split used: heldout-onboarding-2024Q4 (2k prompts). Failure threshold: >0.25 delta in mean appropriateness score vs baseline.
methodology: 1) Compute per-prompt delta vs baseline and tag top 10% worst delta prompts. 2) Cluster those prompts by structural features (input temperature, presence of enumerated lists, system role scaffolds, multi-turn context markers) and embedding similarity. 3) Manually label clusters for 'affinity' types (format/interaction pattern). 4) For each cluster propose hotpatch: prompt-transformer templates, decoding rule overrides, or lightweight reranker insertion. 5) Quick A/B sims with 1k-sample microbench using deterministic seed for reproducibility.
clusters: Cluster A — Instruction-with-lists: user prompts that include explicit list formatting (1., 2., a) and expect concise enumerations; accounts for ~38% of observed delta tokens and 42% of failing samples.

Cluster B — Role-primed multi-turn: prompts that prepend system role text (e.g., 'You are an expert tax advisor') followed by short examples; model returns verbose narrative instead of bulleted output.
Cluster C — Implicit constraint-neglect: prompts that embed constraints (word limit, style) mid-prompt; model ignores constraint and produces long outputs.
Cluster D — Numeric hallucination seeds: prompts requesting numeric summaries or counts from invented data; higher factuality errors and ties to decoding temperature and repetition penalties.
Cluster E — Code-ish pseudo inputs: natural language prompts with inline code-like tokens (backticks, JSON samples) where the model mis-parses structure and outputs malformed code.
Cluster F — Short ambiguous asks: 1-2 token user asks ("Explain X") with insufficient context causing off-topic completions; small but consistent appropriateness drop.
prompt_archetypes: Archetype 1: Bulleted response expected — user supplies numbered list skeleton and short items expected; model expands each item into paragraphs.
Archetype 2: Role + example — single example given then instruction to follow; model overfits to example tone and ignores final instruction variant.
Archetype 3: Inline constraint — e.g., 'In 30 words or less' embedded after the first sentence; often ignored when additional context tokens follow.
Archetype 4: Pseudo-structured input — natural prompts that include code-like delimiters; parser confusion leads to format corruption.
Archetype 5: Numeric synthesis request — asking for counts/estimates without source; model hallucinates confident numbers.
Archetype 6: Minimal prompt — single-token or short headers expecting a summary; model defaults to generic templates causing inappropriateness.
Archetype 7: Mixed-language fragments — small subset where prompts contain two languages; higher likelihood of partial translation or mis-formatting.
Archetype 8: Rewriting tasks with tone constraints — model changes tone incorrectly despite explicit tone markers.
Archetype 9: Instruction chaining — multiple sequential instructions separated by semicolons; model executes first items and drops later constraints.
Archetype 10: List-synthesis requests with examples — expects consistent separator and short forms; model returns nested lists or prose instead.
failure_examples: EX1 (Cluster A): Prompt: 'List three pros of X:\n1.' Model: returns 3-paragraph responses for each item. Expected: 3 short bullet lines. Delta appropriateness: -0.34.

EX2 (Cluster B): Prompt: 'You are an expert HR consultant. When asked to draft an offer letter use professional tone. Example: ... Then: Draft for a contractor.' Model: copies example verbatim and misses contractor-specific terms. Human rating drop: -0.28.
EX3 (Cluster C): Prompt: 'Translate and keep it under 20 words: "...long text..."' Model returns 45 tokens. Cost impact: +32% token use.
EX4 (Cluster E): Prompt contains JSON snippet and asks to 'fix keys'; model returns prose explanation rather than corrected JSON; downstream parser error in 12% of cases.
EX5 (Cluster D): 'How many employees in company X?' Model returns a confident number with no citation; factuality failure.
EX6 (Cluster F): Single token prompt 'Summarize' with no context; model emits generic unrelated summary.
hotpatch_catalog: Hotpatch 1 — Response shape enforcement (low risk): Add a lightweight post-processing layer that enforces max line count and collapses paragraph expansions into bullet tokens when list markers are present. Quick sim: recovers ~65% of Cluster A failures with negligible latency impact (+1-2ms).

Hotpatch 2 — Role calibration prefix (medium risk): For role-primed prompts inject a short clarifying prompt: 'Follow the tone but prioritize concision and task-specific terminology.' Sim reduces overfitting to examples for Cluster B in 1k-sim by 48% but can change style for some ok responses — tag for manual review.

Hotpatch 3 — Constraint sanitizer (low risk): Parse inline constraints (regex for "\\d+ words" / "under X") and rewrite prompt to surface constraint at the start. Restores constraint adherence in ~72% of Cluster C cases.

Hotpatch 4 — Code-structure detector + formatter (medium risk): If inline code markers detected, force the model to emit fenced blocks and run a small validity checker; addresses Cluster E malformed outputs in 80% of trials but adds ~8ms.

Hotpatch 5 — Numeric-skeptic reranker (higher risk): Insert a lightweight factuality classifier for numeric claims and rerank candidate completions preferring hedged language or 'I don't know' when source absent. Reduces numeric hallucinations by 60% but increases false negatives on legitimately correct counts.

Hotpatch 6 — Short-prompt expansion scaffold (low risk): For very short prompts, prepend a clarifying micro-prompt asking for scope (one-shot prompt expansion) or use a canned interpreter that asks a follow-up. Tradeoff: 1-turn latency increase if follow-up triggered.

Hotpatch 7 — Deterministic decoding guard (config change): For list-heavy archetypes, temporarily bias sampling toward lower temperature and higher repetition penalty to avoid verbose expansions. Needs A/B safety checks for overall creativity regressions.
rollout_recommendations: Staged rollout: (1) Deploy Response shape enforcement + Constraint sanitizer (Hotpatch 1 & 3) as safe defaults to 10% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor appropriateness and token usage. (2) If stable, expand to 50% and add Code-structure detector behind a flag. (3) Numeric-skeptic reranker should be canaried only on high-risk customer tenants and monitored for false negatives. Track per-route metrics and prompt-affinity breakouts in the console dashboard.
immediate_actions: Implement Hotpatch 1 and 3 as lightweight transforms in the serving pre/post chain (assigned: Marco).
Create targeted eval harness for Cluster B with 2k synthetic variations to stress role-priming behavior (assigned: Aisha).
Open follow-up JIRA to add prompt-affinity telemetry to onboarding pipeline to automatically surface emerging clusters (JIRA-ML-1478, assigned: Samir).
Run 24h A/B with 10k live samples for shape enforcement to validate latency and conversion metrics (assigned: Nina).
long_term_action_items: Integrate prompt-affinity labels into onboarding model fingerprints to detect drift earlier.
Extend eval rubric to include format adherence and output shape metrics as first-class signals.
Train small adapter tuned for format-sensitive outputs and evaluate as a model-variant fallback for dedicated customers.
Document known archetypes and hotpatch outcomes in Confluence for on-call and solutions teams.
Consider adding a structured-output mode to API that forces schema compliance for customers with strict format needs.
notes_to_self: Next sync with SRE to confirm latency budget for +8ms transforms. Watch out for edge regression where shape enforcement can over-collapse legitimately nuanced responses — keep manual review flag. Capture more examples from customer-123 logs for Cluster B before the next PR.
